note.label: Exodus 8: Frogs, Lice, and Swarms of Flies

precepts.why:
These were no ordinary flies. “For them the bitings of grasshoppers and flies killed, neither was there found any remedy for their life: for they were worthy to be punished by such.”

The swarms of flies were biting and killing men and animals, and no remedy was found; “the land was corrupted by reason of the swarm of flies.” The Egyptians were worthy to be punished by such, while the Lord severed the land of Goshen, where His people dwelt, so that no swarms of flies were there.

precepts.text: Goshen, the best of the land, was given to Israel in Joseph's day; that is where the children of Israel dwelt apart from Egypt.
precepts.point: Goshen was Israel's own quarter in Egypt, where we had our own houses and our own cattle; it was given to us in the days of Joseph, as we read in the book of Genesis.

note.label: Exodus 8: Frogs, Lice, and Swarms of Flies

precepts.why:
“I will sever in that day the land of Goshen, in which my people dwell, that no swarms of flies shall be there”. Goshen was Israel's own quarter in Egypt, where we had our own houses and our own cattle.

It was given to us in the days of Joseph: Pharaoh said, “The land of Egypt is before thee; in the best of the land make thy father and brethren to dwell; in the land of Goshen let them dwell”. That is where the children of Israel dwelt apart from Egypt, and that is where the Lord put a division between His people and Pharaoh's people, so that Pharaoh would know that the Lord is in the midst of the earth.

points: Aaron stretched out his hand over the waters, and the frogs came up and covered the land of Egypt. With this second plague the Most High was mocking Heqet, the Egyptian idol god of the frogs.

note.label: Exodus 8: Frogs, Lice, and Swarms of Flies

points: The magicians did so with their enchantments and brought up frogs, but just as with the water they could only add to the plague; they could not take the frogs away.

note.label: Exodus 8: Frogs, Lice, and Swarms of Flies

points: So Pharaoh called for Moses and Aaron and said, Entreat the Lord that he may take away the frogs. Why did Pharaoh not call on Heqet, the god of frogs? He had to go to the Lord.

note.label: Exodus 8: Frogs, Lice, and Swarms of Flies

points: With the third and fourth plagues, the lice and the swarms of flies, the Most High was mocking Beelzebub, the idol lord of flies and uncleanness.

note.label: Exodus 8: Frogs, Lice, and Swarms of Flies

points: All the dust of the land became lice in man and in beast throughout all the land of Egypt. Imagine that: the dust of the whole land of Egypt turned to lice.

note.label: Exodus 8: Frogs, Lice, and Swarms of Flies

points: The magicians did so with their enchantments to bring forth lice, but this time they could not; and the magicians said unto Pharaoh, This is the finger of God. Yet Pharaoh's heart was hardened.

note.label: Exodus 8: Frogs, Lice, and Swarms of Flies

points: The Lord severed the land of Goshen, where His people dwelt, so that no swarms of flies were there, and put a division between His people and Pharaoh's people, to the end Pharaoh may know that the Lord is in the midst of the earth.

note.label: Exodus 8: Frogs, Lice, and Swarms of Flies

points: Goshen was Israel's own quarter in Egypt, where we had our own houses and our own cattle; it was given to us in the days of Joseph, as we read in the book of Genesis.

note.label: Exodus 8: Frogs, Lice, and Swarms of Flies

points: Pharaoh said, Go sacrifice to your God in the land; but Moses answered, It is not meet, for we should sacrifice the abomination of the Egyptians before their eyes, and will they not stone us? Israel's sacrifices were the very animals Egypt held sacred, so Israel must go three days' journey into the wilderness.

note.label: Exodus 8: Frogs, Lice, and Swarms of Flies

points: Moses warned Pharaoh, Let not Pharaoh deal deceitfully any more. The Lord removed the swarms so that there remained not one; and Pharaoh hardened his heart at this time also, and would not let the people go.
